A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CR/CPU research despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original unlearning experiments on CIFAR-10 and Tiny ImageNet, including baseline evaluations, CPU results, and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original unlearning experiments and adds evaluations on Oxford-Pets, CIFAR-20, additional baselines, and alternative forgetting scenarios.

M1.justification: The CPU objective, epoch-wise calibration-threshold updates, margin, combination with the original loss, and shadow/semi-shadow procedures are unchanged. Renaming Lunlearn to Lcpu and testing additional integrations do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds Oxford-Pets image classification, subclass-wise forgetting on CIFAR-20 derived from CIFAR-100, and worst-case forget sets on CIFAR-10 (Tables 8, 11, and 12). These substantially extend the represented data and forgetting requirements beyond the retained random and class-wise CIFAR-10/Tiny ImageNet evaluations.

E2.justification: SCRUB, LoTUS, and MUNBa join the nine retained methods in corresponding CR comparisons. CPU comparisons also expand to Salun and SFRon on CIFAR-10. Conversely, the MIA recovery comparison contracts from nine methods in v2 Table 6 to RT, FT, and RL in v3 Table 6.

E3.justification: v3 removes MIACR from the evaluation suite and adds experiments using Swin-T and alternative conformal predictors LAC, EntmaxScore, and APS. The shared training budgets, calibration sample counts, and alpha/lambda sweeps remain substantially unchanged. Appendix C newly documents the existing MIA implementation rather than establishing that its protocol changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds CPU loss-integration ablations for Salun and SFRon, training-overhead measurements, and CR sensitivity comparisons across conformal predictors (Tables 7, 9, and 10). Calibration-size and non-conformity-distribution analyses are expanded. The earlier lambda sweeps and shadow-model distribution-shift analysis are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions describe three independent trials and report mean plus standard deviation in the detailed CR tables. No increased run count, new seed disclosure, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is established. Revised standard deviations and additional result rows do not constitute a changed reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for new baselines, datasets, forgetting scenarios, conformal predictors, CPU integrations, and timing, while removing MIACR results. Shared entries also change: in Table 3's 10% Tiny ImageNet/ViT setting, NegGrad+ CR on forget data changes from 2.184 to 1.052 and Salun from 1.311 to 0.528. These are reported score revisions, not evidence of an improved algorithm; the matched CPU appendix table is unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal MIACR definition and its singleton prediction-set criterion in v2 Equation 7 are removed. The SCP, Coverage, Set Size, CR, and CPU-loss mathematics remain unchanged apart from notation and numbering. The newly displayed standard MIA formula supplies explanation rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the principal contribution from addressing UA and MIA through two proposed metrics, CR and MIACR, to addressing UA through CR. CPU remains a central contribution. MIA recovery survives as supporting appendix evidence, but MIACR is no longer a claimed contribution.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes criticizing UA from claiming that retraining itself exhibits fake forgetting, and acknowledges that exchangeability may fail. Appendix F.1 adds substantive qualifications about unsuitable conformal predictors, particularly APS. Conversely, v2's explicit discussion of image-only applicability and calibration-data access in Appendix D is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds baseline implementation descriptions, training budgets for the added methods, a confidence-based SVC membership-attack procedure using balanced retain/test samples, runtime measurements, and a code-availability statement with a repository link. The original hardware, optimizer, and calibration disclosures are retained. This substantially expands reproducibility information without establishing changes to the shared implementations.

R1.justification: v3 expands the earlier Becker–Liebig comparison, adds a substantive distinction from LoTUS's uncertainty-based distillation, and positions MIA/U-MIA as auxiliary evaluations. It also discusses the choice of simple conformal prediction against newer variants and adds relevant unlearning, calibration, and benchmark references. This extends research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and its abstract and introduction are rewritten around CR and fake forgetting. Related work moves before the technical development, calibration discussion moves into the experimental section, and existing appendix material is reorganized into more specialized sections. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions alongside the scientific changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one-column to two-column layout. Comparison tables gain baseline rows and MIA columns; the CPU table is reorganized and brings existing lambda=1 results into the main text. New analyses add displays, MIACR tables disappear, and retained appendix figures and tables are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's CPU evaluation centered on RT, FT, and RL, v3 provides useful tests with additional unlearning methods and Oxford-Pets, plus timing and MIA implementation details. Its retraining and exchangeability qualifications also improve interpretation. These gains are tempered by removal of the explicit limitations discussion and new reporting inconsistencies: the added MUNBa row in Table 3 reports coverage 0.050, set size 0.994, and CR 0.998, inconsistent with Equation 6. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than a substantial overall gain.
